gnaeus julius agricola.d: Roman general who was governor of Britain and extended Roman rule north to the Firth of Forth (37-93)

gnaeus pompeius magnus.d: Roman general and statesman who quarrelled with Caesar and fled to Egypt where he was murdered (106-48 BC)

gnaphalium.d: large widely distributed genus of coarse hairy herbs with whitish involucres

gnaphalium sylvaticum.d: weedy perennial of north temperate regions having woolly foliage and dirty white flowers in a leafy spike

gnarl.d: something twisted and tight and swollen
e: their muscles stood out in knots
the old man's fists were two great gnarls

gnarl.d: make complaining remarks or noises under one's breath
e: she grumbles when she feels overworked

gnarl.d: twist into a state of deformity
e: The wind has gnarled this old tree

gnarled.d: used of old persons or old trees; covered with knobs or knots

gnarly.d: used of old persons or old trees; covered with knobs or knots

gnat.d: any of various small biting flies: midges; biting midges; black flies; sand flies

gnatcatcher.d: very small North American and South American warblers

gnathion.d: the most inferior point of the mandible in the midline

gnathostomata.d: comprising all vertebrates with upper and lower jaws

gnathostome.d: a vertebrate animal possessing true jaws

gnaw.d: bite or chew on with the teeth

gnawer.d: relatively small placental mammals having a single pair of constantly growing incisor teeth specialized for gnawing

gnawing mammal.d: relative large gnawing animals; distinguished from rodents by having two pairs of upper incisors specialized for gnawing

gneiss.d: a laminated metamorphic rock similar to granite

gnetaceae.d: plants having small unisexual flowers and fleshy or winged fruit: in some classifications includes the genera Ephedra and Welwitschia as well as genus Gnetum

gnetales.d: chiefly tropical or xerophytic woody plants; practically unknown as fossils but considered close to the ancestral line of angiosperms

gnetophyta.d: gymnospermous flowering plants; supposed link between conifers and angiosperms; in some systems classified as a class (Gnetopsida) and in others as a subdivision (Gnetophytina or Gnetophyta)

gnetophytina.d: gymnospermous flowering plants; supposed link between conifers and angiosperms; in some systems classified as a class (Gnetopsida) and in others as a subdivision (Gnetophytina or Gnetophyta)

gnetopsida.d: gymnospermous flowering plants; supposed link between conifers and angiosperms; in some systems classified as a class (Gnetopsida) and in others as a subdivision (Gnetophytina or Gnetophyta)

gnetum.d: small tropical tree with tiered branches and divaricate branchlets having broad glossy dark green leaves; exploited for its edible young leaves and seeds that provide a fine flour

gnetum gnemon.d: small tropical tree with tiered branches and divaricate branchlets having broad glossy dark green leaves; exploited for its edible young leaves and seeds that provide a fine flour

gnocchi.d: (Italian) a small dumpling made of potato or flour or semolina that is boiled or baked and is usually served with a sauce or with grated cheese

gnome.d: a short pithy saying expressing a general truth
a legendary creature resembling a tiny old man; lives in the depths of the earth and guards buried treasure

gnomon.d: indicator provided by the stationary arm whose shadow indicates the time on the sundial

gnosis.d: intuitive knowledge of spiritual truths; said to have been possessed by ancient Gnostics

gnostic.d: possessing intellectual or esoteric knowledge of spiritual things

gnosticism.d: a religious orientation advocating gnosis as the way to release a person's spiritual element; considered heresy by Christian churches

gnp.d: former measure of the United States economy; the total market value of goods and services produced by all citizens and capital during a given period (usually 1 yr)

gnu.d: large African antelope having a head with horns like an ox and a long tufted tail

gnu goat.d: large heavily built goat antelope of eastern Himalayan area
